function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to log foods using the tool. They mention earlier consumption (two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee) but we only have logs for current day? We can log both sets. For each entry, need to specify portion amounts and units. Let's assume:

Frozen mango: 8 pieces -> use piece unit. Portion amount 8. Meal type maybe lunch/dinner/snack; unspecified so defaults to snack. Log date could be now if not provided.

Chai tea: likely beverage; no defined unit in tool except cup, tablespoon etc. Use cup. Portion amount 1 cup. Meal type default snack.

Pepperoni pizza slice: 2 slices. Unit slice. Portion amount 2. Meal type default snack.

Coffee: beverage; treat as cup. Portion amount 1 cup. Meal type default snack.

We should call log_food twice per item? Actually one call per item. So total four calls. Provide JSON arguments accordingly. We'll include log_date as today's timestamp. But we don't know exact time; we can omit it because default null means system will fill? It says default null. Might just leave out. We'll provide minimal required fields.
